key_insight: A large randomized controlled trial at ICLR 2025 shows that providing LLM-generated feedback to reviewers makes reviews more informative and increases reviewer–author engagement, demonstrating that LLMs can meaningfully improve peer-review outcomes at scale.
problem_solved: Addresses uneven quality and limited constructiveness in peer review by augmenting reviewer feedback to help authors receive clearer, more actionable critiques and to boost interaction between reviewers and authors.
method: Large-scale randomized controlled study run with reviewers at ICLR 2025 comparing standard reviews versus reviews augmented with LLM-generated feedback.
Intervention: reviewers received LLM-produced suggestions/edits or feedback prompts; outcomes measured via rubric-scored informativeness, engagement metrics (e.g., author replies), and surveys.
Statistical analysis of treatment effects to quantify changes in review quality and reviewer–author engagement.
impact: Shows a practical pathway to scale more constructive, consistent peer review, improving author revision cycles and conference editorial processes; useful for conference organizers, platform builders, and reviewers seeking tool-assisted review workflows.
visual_elements: Study flow diagram showing randomization, control vs. LLM-augmented arms, and outcome measures
Bar chart comparing informativeness and engagement metrics between control and treatment groups
Side-by-side example: raw reviewer comment vs. LLM-augmented comment to illustrate qualitative difference
Timeline or ripple chart showing increased author responses / revision iterations after LLM-augmented reviews
paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
